items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: I interviewed Willie about 1970... So I told him I wanted to interview him about Jelly... So I said I'd be glad to pay him $50 for the interview... He was very nice. He talked for an hour.

ctx.x: How much of him had you collected before you actually met him? Had you on the complete record?

By the time I met him, I had probably three-fourths of his records. I remember when, just by way of introduction, I was just about as bad as Hullsizer, who used to play all the Jelly records for Jelly. You'd take him over to his house, Jelly, over to Hullsizer's house. Hullsizer was a record collector from Ohio and happened to be living in Washington about the 1938 period, too. And he'd play all of these records and ask Jelly who's on this record and, you know, tried to get personnel. Jelly couldn't remember some…
Did he go into your chapter in Jasmine? Or am I thinking of...

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: I never paid any attention to him. Much around New York used to hear him with Bechet

ctx.x: Yeah. So Bill would go down to see Jelly when he moved out there. He was already sick and could hardly play. And Bill would start to get Jelly talking. He'd prod him with things like he'd say, well you're alright but you can't play the stuff like Teddy Wilson. Teddy Wilson, I know you're good for that old time stuff but you can't play that new stuff you can't get around on the piano. Or like Art Tatum and all that. So once it got Jelly so burned up that Jelly said I'll play something those guys can't play and…
